note: Material claims sampled from the v0.1 plan (my own pre-research assumptions), the seed guides, and Composio's docs. 'Corrected' means the original belief was wrong and the guides now say what the source says.

entries.claim: Approval is only needed if you list the app in the App Directory; otherwise distribution is fine.
entries.check: Official Slack changelog and rate-limit docs (quote-checked)
entries.finding: Non-Marketplace commercially distributed apps get conversations.history / conversations.replies limited to 1 request per minute and 15 objects per request. For an agent that reads channels, unlisted distribution is effectively broken. It is also called the Slack Marketplace now, not the App Directory.

entries.claim: Marketplace review is a light, optional step.
entries.finding: Submission requires 10 or more active workspaces (developer sandboxes don't count); review takes up to 10 business days preliminary plus up to 10 weeks functional.

entries.claim: Composio's managed Slack app is a safe default for agents.
entries.finding: Composio says it 'is working on Marketplace review for the managed Slack app', so the managed app is currently non-Marketplace: expect install warnings, admin-approval friction, and likely the non-Marketplace history limits. Whether the 1/min limit applies to it is unknown (neither Slack nor Composio states it).

entries.claim: Any app used by real merchants needs Shopify app review.
entries.finding: Custom distribution (a single store, or stores in one Plus organization) needs no App Store review; only public distribution via the App Store does. Custom apps can no longer be created in the store admin.

entries.claim: A Composio-hosted Shopify connection can be distributed through the App Store like any other app.
entries.check: Composio's Shopify credential guide vs. Shopify App Store requirement 2.3.1 (both quote-checked)
entries.finding: Composio's flow asks the merchant to type their store subdomain; App Store requirements forbid asking for the shop domain and require install to start from Shopify. That is a likely review blocker, but whether a Composio-hosted connection can pass review can only be confirmed by submitting one.

entries.claim: Partner account required just to build.
entries.check: shopify.dev docs (no explicit statement found); hands-on pending
entries.finding: Apps are now created in the Dev Dashboard or Shopify CLI; the exact account requirement is to be confirmed in Manthan's hands-on test.

entries.claim: Approval is light or none for a public OAuth integration.
entries.check: Notion authorization guide vs. Marketplace listing guide (both quote-checked)
entries.finding: Notion's docs contradict each other: the authorization guide says 'The Authorization URL field populates after a public connection is submitted for review', while the Marketplace guide says a connection 'can be used via its OAuth flow without being listed'. Only a hands-on test with a second workspace settles it. The guide says so instead of picking one.

entries.claim: Basic scopes (name, email) mean no review at all.
entries.check: Google brand verification + verification exemptions pages (quote-checked)
entries.finding: There is no scope review, but brand verification applies to show your name/logo (automated in minutes, can fall back to 2-3 business days of manual review). Internal (same Google Cloud organization) and personal-use apps are exempt from verification.

entries.claim: Any restricted Gmail scope means a security assessment.
entries.check: Gmail scopes page (quote-checked); flagged by both plan reviewers
entries.finding: The assessment is triggered when restricted-scope data is stored on or transmitted through servers. That covers a typical server-side agent, but not every restricted-scope app. The guide states the scenario explicitly.

entries.claim: Drafting replies (gmail.compose) is a lighter, sensitive scope.
entries.finding: gmail.compose and gmail.modify are restricted (only gmail.send is sensitive), so an agent that drafts replies is on the security-assessment track.

entries.claim: Testing mode: up to 100 test users; their grants expire after 7 days; unverified apps get 100 users for the project's lifetime.
entries.finding: All three confirmed verbatim; basic profile scopes are exempt from the 7-day expiry.

entries.claim: Using Composio's callback URI is fine for verification.
entries.check: Google: authorized domains must be verified in Search Console (quote-checked) + Composio white-labeling doc
entries.finding: Inferred from two documented facts: Google requires ownership verification of authorized domains, and you can't verify Composio's domain, so route the callback through your own domain (Composio documents a redirect proxy). Neither Google nor Composio states this combination outright; labelled as an inference in the guide.

entries.check: Google docs publish neither; only a vendor report found
entries.finding: Google publishes no cost or duration. Nango reports 5-20 days and roughly $540-$720/year; shown in the guide as 'Reported', not fact.

entries.claim: The redirect URI to register is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add (Composio's Google credential guide).
entries.check: Compared Composio's credential guide, white-labeling doc (…/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback) and KB ('do not copy a callback URI from an old example')
entries.finding: Composio's own docs disagree. Every guide says 'copy the callback URI from your Composio dashboard'. Manthan's hands-on test will record which one the dashboard shows.

entries.claim: Probing the authorize endpoint with a dummy client tells you whether the provider validates client IDs up front.
entries.check: probe_url on 4 providers (recorded in each guide)
entries.finding: Behaviour differs and matters for debugging: Google redirects to an invalid_client error immediately; Slack returns HTTP 200 with an empty page; Shopify redirects to the store's admin login first (a bad client ID only surfaces after the merchant logs in); Notion redirects to a JavaScript install page regardless.

hands_on.what: Agent-written manifest (attempts/slack/manifest.yaml) imported by Manthan; install to own workspace; Composio auth config; screenshot distribution requirements.
Create project, add gmail.readonly and see its label, test-mode consent via Composio, screenshot Verification Center.
Dev Dashboard app + dev store via Composio; screenshot distribution choice; confirm account requirement.
Create a public connection; check whether an authorization URL exists before submitting for review.
Once ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set: re-run the live agent on Gmail, Slack, Shopify and diff its claims against the seed guides.
